messages:
marta (newhire): hey folks, first day stuff - I can't reach the internal feature-flag svc at `ff.internal`. `curl ff` just resolves to public IP. I'm on company VPN (WireGuard split-tunnel) on Fedora. Any quick ideas?

devx: welcome! quick question: are you using the short name `ff` or `ff.internal`? split-tunnel only forwards our internal DNS suffixes, so short names might resolve locally to public entries.

marta (newhire): i've been using `ff` (short). `getent hosts ff` -> 54.23.12.9 (public). `getent hosts ff.internal` -> 10.9.2.45 (private). but the app in my dev container tries `ff` and fails.

nate: two options: 1) update the container /etc/resolv.conf to include `search internal` so short names get suffixed, or 2) add a hosts entry in the container for now. Container DNS is often inherited from host or Docker's embedded DNS, which may not have the search domain.

oncall-sre: also confirm your split-tunnel policy includes the `internal` suffix. if DNS is local it may return public IPs for short names.

marta (newhire): `cat /etc/resolv.conf` in the container shows no search line. host has search `corp.internal`.

kevin: i can push a quick edge change to the dev split-tunnel profile to force `search internal` into DHCP options for WireGuard peers, but i'd prefer a minimal workaround first. try `echo "10.9.2.45 ff" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts` inside the container and restart the app. if that fixes it we'll plan infra change + doc note.

marta (newhire): added hosts entry, app now talks to private ff :tada: thank you.

infra-bot: NET-4201 created: "container DNS search suffix missing for WG peers" assigned to eng-infra.

kevin: follow-ups: (1) infra ticket to add search suffix to DHCP config for peers, (2) update onboarding doc to include the container DNS gotcha and a one-liner `echo "$(getent hosts ff.internal | awk '{print $1}') ff" | sudo tee -a /etc/hosts` for quick fixes, (3) add a small test in bootstrap to verify short-name resolution.

marta (newhire): i'll open the docs PR and add the steps I ran. thanks for the fast help!

devx: added this thread to the new-hire checklist so it's caught during first-login smoke tests. :white_check_mark:
